bio: Senior entrepreneur who co-founder with his brother, then launched Zeta in 2015 to give banks modern, cloud-native infrastructure. Zeta became a unicorn after a $250M SoftBank-led round in 2021.
story:
From Domain Names to Banking Backbones: Bhavin Turakhia's Second Act

Banks were stuck with costly, slow legacy systems, so Bhavin Turakhia built them a cloud-native alternative.

He first co-founded Directi with his brother Divyank, creating BigRock, ResellerClub and LogicBoxes, and the group later saw a reported $900M transaction. In 2015, he launched Zeta with Ramki Gaddipati, offering banks card processing and core banking infrastructure despite entrenched rivals like Fiserv, FIS and Temenos.

Milestones:


- 2015: Zeta founded

- 2021: $250M from SoftBank Vision Fund 2

- ~$1.45B valuation, a unicorn



Takeaway: Sell the plumbing, in the industry where it's oldest, and be patient.

bio: Former ad professional who founded BigTree Entertainment in 1999 and built BookMyShow into India's leading online platform for discovering and booking movies, live events and entertainment.
story:
From Ad Desk to Box Office

Booking entertainment meant traditional ticket counters; Ashish Hemrajani moved it online.

A former ad account manager, he spotted online ticketing while holidaying in South Africa. In 1999 he launched BigTree Entertainment with Parikshit Dar and Rajesh Balpande, later expanding BookMyShow into discovery.

Key milestones:
- 1999: BigTree founded
- 2014: Fortune India 40 Under 40

Takeaway: Ticketing is copyable; owning discovery and the customer relationship isn't.

bio: Former McKinsey consultant who founded InMobi in 2007 and made it India's first unicorn in 2011, then expanded into consumer technology with Glance, focused on AI-powered content and commerce.
story:
From Boardrooms to Billion-Dollar Mobile Ads

As smartphones changed how people go online, Naveen Tewari built an advertising business for the mobile era.

A McKinsey alum with an IIT Kanpur degree and a Harvard MBA, he founded InMobi in 2007. By 2011 it was India's first unicorn. He then pivoted into consumer tech with Glance, bringing content and commerce closer to users.

Key milestones:
- 2007: InMobi founded
- 2011: India's first unicorn
- 2013: IIT Kanpur Distinguished Alumnus Award

Takeaway: Catch the platform shift early, then reinvent before the shift matures.

bio: Co-founder and Managing Director of upGrad, the higher-education and professional-learning company he launched in 2015 with Ronnie Screwvala and Phalgun Kompalli. He leads strategy, partnerships and international expansion.
story:
From Consulting to Classrooms Without Walls

Working professionals needed new skills without leaving their careers; Mayank Kumar helped bring that education online.

After roles at Bertelsmann and The Parthenon Group, he co-founded upGrad in 2015 with Ronnie Screwvala and Phalgun Kompalli. He drove strategy, partnerships and international expansion, building university ties that gave programmes credibility.

Key milestones:
- 2015: upGrad founded
- 2021: $120M and $210M funding rounds

Takeaway: In education, partnerships open doors; outcomes keep them open.

bio: Co-founder, Executive Director and COO of Urban Company (formerly UrbanClap), the home-services marketplace he co-founded in 2014. He oversees operations across its services and products businesses in India and overseas.
story:
From Local Referrals to a Listed Marketplace

Home services ran on word-of-mouth; Varun Khaitan helped turn them into a trusted, bookable platform.

After Qualcomm and BCG, he co-founded UrbanClap in 2014 with Abhiraj Bhal and Raghav Chandra, running operations as it scaled. Rebranded Urban Company in 2020, it added its Native products business and went public in 2025.

Key milestones:
- 2021: $190M raised at ~$2B valuation
- 2025: ₹1,900 crore IPO
- FY25: ₹1,144 crore revenue, ₹240 crore net profit

Takeaway: Marketplaces win on consistency, not listings. Control the quality and trust follows.

bio: Founder and CEO of OYO Rooms, the budget-hotel platform he built after dropping out of college at 17. His first venture, Oravel Stays (2012), was relaunched as OYO (On Your Own) and expanded beyond India.
story:
The College Dropout Who Rebuilt Budget Stays

Budget travelers in India paid hotel prices that didn't match the service; Ritesh Agarwal set out to fix that.

A frequent traveler who had lived in many hotels, he dropped out of college at 17 and launched Oravel Stays in 2012. He later relaunched it as OYO (On Your Own), taking the brand beyond India, including China.

Key milestones:
- 2012: Oravel Stays launched
- 2015: OYO Rooms founded
- 12,000+ properties across 800 cities (per source)

Takeaway: A customer's frustration is a market signal. When the first version isn't the one, relaunch it.

bio: Co-founder of Flipkart, which he started in 2007 with Binny Bansal from a small apartment in Bangalore. Flipkart grew into one of India's leading e-commerce platforms.
story:
Two Founders, One Apartment, One E-commerce Giant

Two young entrepreneurs set out to build an online store for India, starting from a small Bangalore apartment.

Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal co-founded Flipkart in 2007 and grew it into one of the country's leading e-commerce platforms, one that now employs over 35,000 people.

Key milestones:
- 2007: Flipkart founded in Bangalore
- Valued at over $15B (per source)
- 35,000+ employees
- 2016: TIME 100 recognition

Takeaway: Start small, but build for scale. A spare apartment can host a national brand.

bio: Co-founder of Mamaearth, the toxin-free D2C beauty brand she started in 2016 with her husband Varun Alagh. Parent company Honasa Consumer now runs six brands and listed on the NSE and BSE in October 2023.
story:
From a Mother's Worry to a Listed Beauty Brand

When her son's eczema flared with every baby-care product on the shelf, Ghazal Alagh decided to make a safer one.

She researched ingredients and tested formulations with about 700 mothers before co-founding Mamaearth in 2016 with husband Varun, starting with Rs 25 lakh and seven toxin-free baby-care products. The company grew into Honasa Consumer, with six brands.

Key milestones:
- 2016: Mamaearth founded with Rs 25 lakh
- 2022: Became a unicorn
- Oct 2023: Honasa listed, raising Rs 1,701 crore
- FY23: Rs 1,492.7 crore revenue

Takeaway: Solve a problem you personally feel, and test it with the people who share it before you scale.

bio: Co-founder and CEO of Hopper, the Montreal-based travel app that predicts and books flights and hotels at the best prices. He pivoted it from a blog aggregator into a mobile-first business with $1B+ in sales.
story:
The Pivot That Turned a Blog Aggregator into a Travel Giant

Travelers never knew when to book; Frederic Lalonde built an app that predicts the best price.

Hopper began in 2007 aggregating travel blogs, but growth stalled despite funding. Its real asset was data. After airfare research went viral in 2014, traffic jumped 100x, and Lalonde cut his 15-person team nearly in half and relaunched as a mobile-only app in 2015.

Key milestones:
- 2007: Hopper founded in Montreal
- 35M+ app installs
- $1B+ in sales
- $235M raised

Takeaway: Your stalled product may be hiding your real one. Mine the data it leaves behind.

bio: Co-founder and CEO of Deel, the platform for contracts, payments, employer of record and payroll for companies hiring across borders. He built it with Shuo Wang after a ten-day pivot before Y Combinator demo day in 2019.
story:
The Ten-Day Pivot Behind a $1B Payroll Platform

Paying people across borders meant slow transfers, legal forms and shifting tax rules; Alex Bouaziz built one platform to handle it all.

Deel began as an escrow tool for freelancers, and nobody cared: contractors don't choose how they get paid, their clients do. A Y Combinator batchmate used it for contracts and international payments instead. Ten days before demo day in March 2019, Bouaziz and co-founder Shuo Wang rebuilt around contracts.

Key milestones:
- Mar 2019: 290 contractors, $5,000/month at demo day
- Jun 2025: $1B revenue run rate (company-stated)
- Oct 2025: $300M raised at a $17.3B valuation

Takeaway: Build for the side of the transaction that holds the budget, then listen to who uses it sideways.

bio: Solo founder who left her corporate job in 2009 and built an online course business around live-launched digital course. Her flagship, Digital Course Academy, has been relaunched every year since 2019.
story:
From a $267 Flop to a $120M Course Business

Her first course launch made $267; Amy Porterfield turned that failure into a playbook for launching digital courses.

After quitting her corporate job in 2009, she launched to an email list of about 600 people she had never emailed. The pitch fell flat. She rebuilt by repeating: one signature course, relaunched again and again, growing from $30,000 to nearly $1M in a single launch. In 2019 she launched Digital Course Academy.

Key milestones (self-reported):
- 2009: Business started
- 2015: ~$1M launch, 1,500+ new members
- 2019: Digital Course Academy launched
- 2025: $120M in course revenue, 100,000+ students

Takeaway: List size isn't the variable; relationships are. Repeat one winner instead of chasing new ideas.

bio: Co-founder of FlapTrip, an AI travel planner that turns your preferences into a day-by-day itinerary with real places and mapped routes in about 60 seconds. She built it on nights and weekends alongside a full-time job.
story:
Eleven Months of Nights and Weekends to Three Paying Users

Planning a 21-day Germany road trip took Ana Vershinina two months of evenings; she built an app to do it in 60 seconds.

With two co-founders and full-time jobs, she built FlapTrip after hours. Six months of planned work became eleven, and burnout hit three months before launch. Eleven days after the App Store release in March 2026, she had 700 installs and three PRO subscribers, mostly friends and family, and she publicly shared what went wrong.

Key milestones:
- 26 Mar 2026: App Store launch (Android followed 31 Mar)
- 1,000+ on the waitlist, 60,000+ destinations covered
- 11 days post-launch: 700 installs, 3 PRO subscribers

Takeaway: Early installs from friends measure goodwill, not demand. Track everything from day one.

bio: Co-founder and CEO of Airbnb, the marketplace where people rent out homes and spare rooms to travellers. It began in 2007 as three airbeds in a San Francisco apartment and listed on Nasdaq in December 2020.
story:
Three Airbeds, Three Launches, One Global Marketplace

When a design conference sold out every San Francisco hotel, Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia turned three airbeds into a place to stay.

Paying guests came within a week, then a year of nothing: three launches, credit-card debt, election-themed cereal, and investors who said no or went silent. Y Combinator in 2009 changed that. Airbed & Breakfast became Airbnb and went public in December 2020.

Key milestones:
- Oct 2007: First paying guests
- Mar 2009: Renamed Airbnb
- Dec 2020: Nasdaq listing
- 2025: $12.2B in revenue

Takeaway: A fast first sale isn't a business. Persistence through a year of no is.

bio: Co-founder of CROSSNET, the first four-way volleyball net, which he started in 2017 with his brother Greg and friend Mike Delpapa. He bootstrapped it with $7,000 from his 401k, and it was acquired by Vivere in 2025.
story:
$7,000, a Trunk, and a Four-Way Volleyball Net

Volleyball was a two-team game; Chris Meade and two friends built a cross-shaped net for four.

He pulled about $7,000 from his 401k for the first inventory and sold nets from his car trunk on Miami's beaches, about one a day, with no investors. In 2019, a viral clip from a European player sold out retailers within 72 hours and opened doors at Scheels and Dick's. CROSSNET was acquired by Vivere in August 2025.

Key milestones (founder-reported):
- 2017: CROSSNET started
- 5,000+ stores
- $35M+ in revenue
- Aug 2025: Acquired by Vivere

Takeaway: Put your product in people's hands in person, and track every dollar daily.

bio: Founder of YourStory, one of India's most recognised media platforms for entrepreneurs and startups. She launched it in 2008, at just 23.
story:
The 23-Year-Old Who Gave Indian Startups a Voice

Indian entrepreneurs, young and old, needed a platform to tell their stories; Shradha Sharma built one.

She launched YourStory in 2008, aged just 23. It grew into one of India's most respected media brands, covering entrepreneurship, startups and business news.

Key milestones:
- 2008: YourStory launched
- Age 23 at founding
- Now a leading startup media platform in India

Takeaway: Serve a community's story and you earn its trust. In media, trust is the business.

bio: Founder and CEO of Ola Cabs, which he launched in 2010 and grew into one of India's most popular ride-sharing platforms. He left a well-paying job at Microsoft to build it.
story:
The Microsoft Exit That Put India's Cabs on a Smartphone

Hailing a cab in India was a hassle; Bhavish Aggarwal made it a tap on a phone.

He left a well-paying job at Microsoft to build Ola Cabs, launched in 2010. Most people thought it was a bad idea, but he kept going until it worked. Ola became one of India's most commonly used ride-sharing platforms.

Key milestones:
- 2010: Ola Cabs launched
- Left Microsoft to scale the idea
- Now one of India's top ride-sharing platforms

Takeaway: When most people call an idea bad, ask whether they've felt the problem. Conviction needs a real pain point behind it.

bio: Founder of Paytm, the Indian digital payments platform he launched in August 2010. It is best known for its mobile wallet, QR-code payments and bill payments, and is part of the One97 group.
story:
From Aligarh to India's Digital Wallet

Paying for things in India meant cash and queues; Vijay Shekhar Sharma put a wallet on the phone.

A native of Aligarh and a Delhi College of Engineering graduate, he worked on several projects and startups before committing to entrepreneurship. He founded Paytm in August 2010 under One97, offering mobile-wallet payments, QR codes and simple bill payments that made it a household name in India.

Key milestones:
- Aug 2010: Paytm founded
- Mobile wallet, QR payments and bill pay at scale
- Expanded into debit cards, a payment gateway and merchant point-of-sale

Takeaway: Make the hard thing, paying, as easy as a tap, and adoption follows.

bio: Co-founder of Zomato, the restaurant discovery platform he started in 2008 with Pankaj Chaddah from his apartment in Delhi.
story:
From a Delhi Apartment to a Global Restaurant Platform

Finding a good restaurant nearby meant guesswork; Deepinder Goyal and Pankaj Chaddah built a place to find, compare and review them.

After working on other projects, they started Zomato in 2008 from Goyal's Delhi apartment. Users quickly took to it. They credit their growth to constant experimentation and close attention to user feedback.

Key milestones (as reported in 2016):
- 2008: Zomato founded
- 50M+ users
- 1M+ restaurants listed
- 22 countries

Takeaway: Listen to users more than you plan. Fast feedback loops beat big plans.
